 At Gwalior

sentences.text:
Laxman Jatav
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh And Others
 Appearance:
Shri Shriratna Nigam, learned counsel for the petitioner.
Shri D.S.Kushwaha, learned Additional Advocate General for r  No.1/State.
Shri Kamlesh Kumar, learned counsel for respondents no.2 an  ORDER 1.

The present petition has been preferred by petitioner under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 for quashing of FIR bearing Crime No.222/2021 registered at Police Station Girwai,
District Gwalior for the offence punishable under Sections 363, 366A, 376 of IPC and Section 3/4 of POCSO Act as well as entire consequential proceedings arising out of the same.
2. Petitioner and respondent No.2 got married on their own volition.
They are living together peacefully in their household.
They were referred to Principal Registrar of this Court to ink down their identity and intent and both have expressed their desire to settle the matter.
Therefore, they filed applications vide I.A. No.16345/2024 and I.A. No.16346/2024 for compounding the offence on the basis of compromise.
3. Prosecutrix and petitioner were appeared before this Court earlier and expressed their desire to settle the matter by compounding the offence.
Specific query was being made by this Court and it was found that both the parties want to settle the dispute and are ready to bury the hatchet, if any.

Therefore, this Court referred the matter before the Principal Registrar NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-GWL:13597 2 MCRC-23443-2024 of this Court for verification of compromise.

sentences.text: the said authority both the parties appeared and expressed their desire to settle their case.
The report of the Principal Registrar is attached with the petition.
4. Counsel for the respondent/State opposed the prayer.
However, could not dispute the factum regarding compromise.
5. Counsel for the respondent No.2 and 3 supported the petitioner's submission.

6. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the documents appended thereto.
7.
This is a case where petitioner and prosecutrix shared emotional and physical proximity.
At the instance of father of prosecutrix, case was registered against petitioner.
Prosecutrix left her maternal home on her own volition.

Although, at the relevant point of time, prosecutrix was minor and was at the cusp of attaining majority but later on she attained majority and thereafter prosecutrix and petitioner entered into wedlock.
They earlier appeared before this Court as well as before Principal Registrar of this Court and expressed their desire for settlement.

8. Be that as it may.
9.
Fact remains that the petitioner and respondent no.3/prosecturix are married couple and both are living in same household.
It is regular and easy to be retributive but at the same time a Judge has to sublimely feel the pulse of the case.
One cannot forget that "Every "F I L E" with same alphabets, contains a "L I F E".

(See : In Re State of Madhya Pradesh Vs. Pankaj Mishra, 2021 SCC OnLine MP 5480 and Geeta Paliwal and others Vs. Sitaram and others reported as 2023 SCC Online MP 811.).
10.

sentences.text: Here "FILE" before this Court carries not only a "LIFE" but many LIVES.

11. Therefore, applications vide I.A. No.16345/2024 and I.A. No.16346/2024 are hereby allowed and this Court under the obtaining facts and circumstances of the case intends to tread on the path of reformative or at least other than retributive one because:-
(i) A girl of tender age around (16-17 years) has fallen in love with a boy of (23-24)
years and driven by hormones they shared emotional and physical NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-GWL:13597 3 MCRC-23443-2024 proximity and moved out of social/legal limits.
( ii )
Girl was of the consistent view that she shared emotional/physical proximity on her own volition and she left her maternal home voluntarily.

Her statements under Section 161 and 164 Cr.P.C.
indicate so.
(iii) Petitioner and prosecutrix entered into wedlock and girl/prosecutrix is living peacefully with her husband.
In case of any punishment, petitioner may have to go to jail and that would disrupt the family forever.

sentences.text: (iv) Both the parties appeared before the Principal Registrar of this Court and inked down their intent and identity repeatedly.

Therefore, in the cumulative facts and circumstances of the case,
matter deserves consideration.
(v) Petitioner does not have any previous criminal background so as to infer any mischief at this juncture.
Therefore, keeping this spirit, this Court intends to inject " L I F E" into this "F I L E" in the interest of justice.

12. Resultantly, the petition stands allowed and FIR bearing Crime No.222/2021 registered at Police Station Girwai, District Gwalior for the offence punishable under Sections 363, 366A, 376 of IPC and Section 3/4 of POCSO Act as well as entire consequential proceedings arising therefrom stand quashed.
Petitioner is set free.

But an expectation can certainly be raised by this Court that petitioner and respondent No.3/prosecutrix shall live peacefully and would try to attain nuptial bliss so that family and social harmony can be maintained.
13.
Petition stands disposed of.

(ANAND PATHAK) JUDGE Ashish*
